title: Structured Logging and Correlation IDs
description: Implement structured logging and correlation IDs in ASP.NET Core to trace requests across services and make production debugging faster and more reliable.

data.text: Structured logging turns free-text messages into queryable data by emitting key-value pairs instead of plain strings. Combined with **correlation IDs**, every log line from a single request shares an identifier, so you can filter, search, and reconstruct what happened across controllers, middleware, and downstream services.

ASP.NET Core's built-in `ILogger` supports structured messages through format strings. When you write `"Order {OrderId} created"`, the logging provider emits both the message template and the `OrderId` as a separate field. Serilog, Seq, and Elasticsearch can index and query these fields.

data.title: Structured Log with Scopes
data.content: Use logging scopes to attach request-level data to every log line emitted inside the scope.

data.text: The .NET `Activity` class automatically creates a trace ID for each incoming request. You can expose this as a correlation ID in log scopes, HTTP response headers, and outbound messages. Some APIs also accept an incoming `X-Correlation-ID` header and continue the same trace rather than starting a new one.

data.title: Correlation ID Middleware
data.content: Add or propagate a correlation ID header on every request and include it in all logs.

terms.definition: A unique identifier shared across logs, traces, and messages for a single request or workflow.
The .NET type representing an operation with a start time, duration, tags, and trace identifiers.
A logical grouping of log messages so shared properties appear on every line emitted inside the scope.

data.title: Avoid Logging Secrets
data.text: Never log passwords, tokens, or credit card numbers. Structured logging makes it easy to accidentally log the entire request body. Use filters or enrichers to scrub sensitive fields before they reach your sink.

data.title: Logging Best Practices
items: Log at the right level: Trace for diagnostics, Debug for development, Information for business events, Warning for recoverable issues, Error for failures.
Include trace ID, user ID, and request path in every structured log scope.
Use a consistent timestamp format and machine-readable log output.
Centralize logs with Seq, Elasticsearch, or Application Insights so you can search by correlation ID.

data.title: Key Takeaway
points: Structured logging makes logs searchable and filterable instead of noisy text blobs.
Correlation IDs tie together logs, traces, and messages for a single request.
Use Activity and logging scopes to attach trace identifiers automatically.
Scrub sensitive data before it reaches your log sink.
data.takeaway: Good logging is not about more text. It is about the right fields in the right format, so you can answer questions in seconds instead of hours.
